facts.text: Sapphire Ridge grew in the late 1960s when Yaras' Sapphire Village, Inc. marketed lots to gem seekers on former Yogo mine tailings.
The community’s name echoes the nearby Yogo Gulch, about 11 miles away, where sapphire mining once thrived.
Sapphire Ridge sits on the west side of the Judith River valley, where flat plains meet the Little Belt Mountains.
Pigeye Road, the main route out of Sapphire Ridge, stretches 10 miles northeast to Utica and southwest into the Little Belt Mountains.
Sapphire Ridge’s sapphires are prized for natural clarity and uniform color, drawing hobbyists since the 1890s after commercial mining ceased.
Geologically, Sapphire Ridge lies within the Judith Basin, underlain by Cretaceous shale, sandstone, and coal-bearing strata from ancient river floodplains.
